title: The Rise of Temujin
description: 1186-1206. Follow Temujin's unification of the Mongol tribes on the steppe: rescue his wife Borte from the Merkits, forge and then break the alliance with Jamukha, defeat the Naiman confederation, and be proclaimed Genghis Khan at the kurultai. The player begins with a small warband and must grow through raids, alliances, and decisive battles.

anachronisms_found: Tayang Khan of the Naiman is represented by the generic European KING unit (crowned monarch on a throne-like frame) — avoidable, since the engine's Genghis Khan campaign supplies Kushluk, a Naiman prince (son of Tayang Khan), as a mounted hero far better suited to a steppe confederation leader
GUARD_TOWER x2 in the enemy camp: the Merkit/Naiman nomads of the 12th-century steppe built no masonry fortifications; a palisade or outpost would have been the period-appropriate choice

The player's hero is the GENGHIS_KHAN unit throughout a scenario that opens in 1186 and ends with the 1206 proclamation — the title is used two decades before it was granted, though the engine offers no 'Temujin' alternative and this is the least-bad pick

Jamukha has no unit representation at all: his alliance and betrayal are handled purely by CHANGE_OWNERSHIP on the same Player Two roster, so the Merkit raiders, Jamukha's Jadaran and the Naiman are materially indistinguishable
Toghrul/Wang Khan of the Kereit, without whose troops the historical rescue of Borte and the Naiman campaign are unintelligible, is entirely absent as player, unit or dialogue

issues_found: Tayang Khan of the Naiman is represented by the generic KING unit — a European monarch model on foot, wholly out of place on the steppe. The engine ships steppe-appropriate heroes (e.g. Kushluk, a Mongol-era cavalry archer hero) or a renamed cavalry archer would have served; a throne-room King is an avoidable error.

Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the Archery Ranges, Stables, Guard Towers and Towers may render in Western European, Mediterranean or East Asian architecture rather than Central Asian; Mongols (or at minimum a nomadic-set civ) was available and should have been assigned to both sides.

Only two players exist, so the Merkits, Jamukha's Jadaran and the Naiman confederation are all the same opponent. The dramatic core of the brief — an alliance forged and then broken — is reduced to a CHANGE_OWNERSHIP trigger rather than a real allied third party turning hostile.
Jamukha himself has no representative unit at all; he exists only in dialogue text. A renamed cavalry archer or a second hero would have cost nothing.

No Merkit, Jamukha or Naiman-specific force differentiation: Player 2 fields one undifferentiated pool of 8 cavalry archers and 10 light cavalry that must stand in for three separate confederations across twenty years.
Borte is presumably the single VILLAGER_FEMALE fetched by BRING_OBJECT_TO_AREA — functional, but unnamed and indistinguishable from any other villager.
Guard Towers for a Merkit/Naiman steppe camp are anachronistic fortification for nomadic pastoralists; yurts and palisade would have been the honest choice.
Chronology is loose: Borte's abduction and rescue occurred c.1184, before the stated 1186 opening, and the Naiman were crushed in 1204, two years before the kurultai.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the Mongols civ (which the engine ships, with its own architecture and cavalry-archer bonuses) is not used; the archery ranges, stables and guard towers may render as West European or Middle Eastern buildings on a Mongolian steppe map.

Three historically distinct opponents — the Merkits, Jamukha's Jadaran, and the Naiman confederation — are collapsed into a single Player 2 whose roster never changes, so the player fights the same warband under three different names.

Jamukha, the blood-brother whose betrayal is the emotional core of the brief, exists only as dialogue and a CHANGE_OWNERSHIP trigger; no unit (not even a renamed cavalry archer) represents him, though the engine allows exactly that.
Tayang Khan of the Naiman is represented by the KING unit, a sceptred European monarch on foot; a renamed cavalry archer or light cavalry would have been the more plausible steppe khan.

Toghrul / Wang Khan of the Kereit is entirely absent, yet his patronage of Temujin and the 1203 war against him were the decisive step before the Naiman campaign — the narration jumps straight from Jamukha to Tayang Khan.
The alliance with Jamukha is triggered AFTER Borte's rescue; in the sources Jamukha and Toghrul supplied the army that carried out the rescue, so the causal order is inverted.
All the dialogue beats and enemy attacks fire on TIMERs rather than on player accomplishment, so the 1186-1206 arc plays out on a clock regardless of what the player does.
Only one female villager on Player 2's side stands for Borte, and nothing marks her; the BRING_OBJECT_TO_AREA rescue works but relies on the player guessing which unit she is.
